messages:
ellie (NebulaForms): hey team — starting ~03:10 UTC our p99 on /v1/embeddings jumped from ~320ms to ~3s, p95 also up. no code deploys on our side. seeing 500s and a few 429s. can you check?

jordan (support): sorry about that — looking now. can you share an example request id when you saw the 500? any change in batch size or seq lengths?

ellie (NebulaForms): req id 6b7f2c3a, we batch 16, inputs are long (avg ~12k tokens) for long-doc search. no config changes on our end.

maria (eng-sre): grabbing traces for tenant=nebulaforms and timeframe 2024-06-20T03:05-03:20Z. preliminary: spike correlates with a set of large streaming requests from tenant "atlas-labs" that started around 03:08. looks like KV-cache churn + large attention memory causing GPU scheduling delays — causing tail blowup for co-located tenants.

alex (eng-runtime): confirmed. sample tail from runtime logs:
```
2024-06-20T03:09:12Z runtime[pid=4123] WARN tenant=nebulaforms req=6b7f2c3a latency=3120ms cause=kv_cache_eviction competing_tenant=atlas-labs tokens=11500
2024-06-20T03:09:13Z runtime[pid=4123] INFO tenant=atlas-labs req=7a9d8f2b streaming=true seq_len=12000 alloc=3.2GiB
```

jordan (support): ops-bot — can we rate-limit atlas-labs for now and apply a temporary reservation for nebulaforms?

ops-bot: acknowledged. creating mitigation ticket. (ticket: MIT-1142)

maria (eng-sre): mitigation plan I'm applying now: 1) apply soft throttle to atlas-labs (drop to 30 rps long-stream) 2) add nebulaforms to a short-lived reservation (2 x baseline slots) to reduce noisy neighbor impact 3) create allowlist entry so nebulaforms bypasses fairshare for 30m while we validate. doing step 1 & 2.

alex (eng-runtime): commands I'm running:
```bash
# reduce long-streamers for atlas-labs
rbctl tenant throttle set --tenant atlas-labs --policy long_stream --rate 30rps --duration 60m
# reserve capacity for nebulaforms
rbctl reservation create --tenant nebulaforms --gpus 2 --duration 60m --reason "emergency tail mitigation"
```

deploy-bot: reservation created id=resv-8791 by alex.

maria (eng-sre): after throttle + reservation applied, p99 dropped to ~420ms at 03:18 and errors subsided. ongoing monitoring.

jordan (support): ellie — can you confirm whether latency looks better on your side?

ellie (NebulaForms): seeing much better numbers now (p99 ~440ms). thanks! quickly: can we get a permanent solution? this happens once a week when another tenant runs huge streaming jobs.

maria (eng-sre): long-term options: 1) recommend dedicated reservation for NebulaForms (monthly commit) 2) per-tenant isolation on inference nodes (placement constraints) 3) automatic detection -> proactive soft-reservations for heavy long-stream tenants 4) improve KV eviction heuristics to prefer evicting from heavy noisy sessions first.

alex (eng-runtime): opened infra ticket INF-2027 to explore placement and preemptible reservations. also adding telemetry to flag "long_streamers" earlier.

jordan (support): next steps for customer: a) offer 2-week emergency reserved trial at reduced rate b) add NebulaForms to an allowlist for emergency bypass during incidents (they approved) c) follow-up call to discuss purchase/reservation. ellie — want me to start the trial and schedule call?

ellie (NebulaForms): yes please on both. also can you send repro steps for our devs so they can try smaller batches while we decide on reserve?

maria (eng-sre): repro steps we used to replicate:
```
# simulate long streaming embed workload (heavy seq lengths)
for i in {1..16}; do \
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings -d '{"input":"'$(printf 'x%.0s' {1..12000})'"}' &
done
# observe p99 in console and runtime traces
```

alex (eng-runtime): short-term config recs for NebulaForms: reduce batch size from 16->8, limit max_seq to 8k tokens client-side, and enable streaming_chunk=2k to avoid very long single-stream requests.

ops-bot: mitigation rule applied to atlas-labs (throttle) and reservation active for nebulaforms until 2024-06-20T04:20Z.

jordan (support): closing loop: created support ticket CS-4982 for trial + billing adjustment, and scheduled engineering follow-up for INF-2027. will keep this thread open for any regressions. :thumbsup:

ellie (NebulaForms): thanks all, really appreciate the fast response. feel free to ping if you need more logs. :raised_hands:
